executiveSummary: Navigation risk remains a key concern: Government advisories note continuing GPS disruption in multiple regions and reinforce that AIS is open and spoofable; mariners should avoid relying on AIS for collision avoidance and report anomalies to NAVCEN. Confidence: High. Government Advisory Port and terminal cyber exposure: Advisory highlights risk from foreign-manufactured port equipment, remotely serviceable ship-to-shore cranes, and logistics platforms such as LOGINK and Nuctech, recommending segmentation, patching, access control, and recovery planning; alignment with USCG directives is emphasized. Confidence: High. Government Advisory Operational picture: No new confirmed maritime cyber incidents, exploitable CVEs, or malware campaigns were identified in the recent 10-day window of the provided feed. This reduces immediate incident-response pressure but does not diminish the strategic risks above. Confidence: Medium. Outlook: Continued reports of GNSS interference and growing scrutiny of port OT supply-chain dependencies are likely. Bridge teams should heighten cross-checks of position sources; ports should review remote access and segmentation controls for cranes and terminal OT. Confidence: Medium. Facts above are drawn from government advisories; judgments synthesize risk relevance for maritime operations and do not assert new incidents absent source confirmation.
keyFindings: GPS disruption persists across multiple regions; AIS remains spoofable and should not be used as a primary collision-avoidance sensor. View Advisory
Foreign-manufactured port technologies and remotely serviceable cranes introduce notable cyber exposure to IT/OT; segmentation, access control, and patching are priority defenses. View Advisory
No new exploitable CVEs, malware, or actor campaigns specific to maritime OT were identified in the supplied reporting window.

topThreats.title: 1) GPS/GNSS disruption and AIS spoofing risks to global navigation
topThreats.action: Loss or manipulation of GNSS position can degrade ECDIS and conning displays; AIS spoofing can distort traffic awareness and VTS picture.

topThreats.title: 2) Cyber exposure from foreign-manufactured port equipment and logistics platforms
topThreats.action: Remotely serviceable cranes and integrated logistics platforms can expand adversary access pathways into terminal OT, impacting cargo flow and safety systems.

events.title: Global GPS disruption and AIS spoofing risks (MARAD 2026-008)
events.text: Assessment: Advisory reiterates GPS disruption affecting maritime navigation in multiple regions and emphasizes AIS spoofability; AIS must not be relied upon for collision avoidance. Maritime domains: Navigation, Bridge systems, VTS interface. Affected systems: GNSS receivers, ECDIS, AIS transceivers, conning displays. Impacts: Possible navigation and safety effects; potential supply-chain delay if traffic management degrades. Recommended actions: Cross-check position sources; report disruptions to NAVCEN; leverage maritime cybersecurity resources.

events.title: Foreign technological, physical, and cyber influence in maritime infrastructure (MARAD 2026-007)
events.text: Assessment: Advisory warns that foreign-manufactured port equipment, logistics platforms (e.g., LOGINK), and remotely serviceable ship-to-shore cranes can expose terminal IT/OT to cyber risk; recommends segmentation, patching, access-control scrutiny, traffic validation, and recovery planning; encourages compliance with USCG directives for PRC-manufactured cranes. Maritime domains: Ports, Terminals, Logistics. Affected systems: Crane OT controls, terminal networks, logistics IT, screening/inspection systems (e.g., Nuctech). Impacts: Possible safety and operational disruption; potential supply-chain impacts from crane downtime and yard congestion. Recommended actions: Strengthen IT/OT boundaries, restrict vendor remote access (with MFA and allow-listing), monitor east-west traffic, maintain tested backups, and patch supported components.
